- architect: Designs system architecture and module boundaries before coding (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- backtesting-verifier: Reviews backtests for lookahead bias, data leakage, survivorship bias, overfitting, and implementation realism. Use after any strategy or backtest code change before trusting the results or promoting to paper/live trading. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- cicd-safety-auditor: Reviews CI/CD pipelines for flight software and safety-critical systems. Checks build reproducibility, artifact traceability, qualified vs unqualified tool separation, and compliance with DO-178C toolchain requirements. Use before any CI/CD configuration change or toolchain update. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- cpp-cmake-specialist: Handles C++17 implementation and CMake build system for the Silmulator's simulation core. Knows the project's C++ conventions, CMake structure, Python binding patterns, and performance-sensitive areas. Use for any C++ core or build system change. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob)

- cross-platform-checker: Catches platform-specific assumptions that work on one OS but break on another — path separators, line endings, filesystem case sensitivity, platform APIs, shell assumptions. Use before any code that will run on both Mac and Linux (or Windows/Mac/Linux). (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- dependency-auditor: Checks that declared dependencies match actual usage across requirements.txt, CMakeLists.txt, package.json, and imports. Flags undeclared dependencies, unused declared dependencies, version drift, and security vulnerabilities in the dependency graph. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- deploy-checker: Verifies that a build actually produced the expected deliverables before declaring success — DMG built, installer works, web files render, binaries execute. Catches the class of failures where the build "succeeded" but didn't produce the thing you needed. (Tools: Read, Bash, Glob)

- devops-pipeline-reviewer: Reviews automation scripts, deployment pipelines, and infrastructure-as-code for reliability, idempotency, rollback safety, and audit trail quality. Specific to flight software DevOps concerns — not generic CI/CD advice. Use before any pipeline or infra change. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- execution-auditor: Reviews order management system (OMS) code for correct handling of fills, partial fills, cancels, and edge cases around market open/close. Use before any OMS change or when connecting to a new execution venue. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- explorer: Maps unfamiliar codebases and reports findings concisely (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- game-state-auditor: Reviews NPC action handling code to ensure proposed actions cannot corrupt game state. Focuses on the trust boundary between LLM output and C++ execution, validation logic, and edge cases in the action system. Use before merging any change to NPC action handling or the dialogue schema. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- hardware-spec-researcher: Given a real device model name, finds its SCPI command set from its programming manual and formats it for implementation in Silmulator. Use before implementing a new real-device simulator to ensure the command set is accurate. (Tools: Read, Write, Glob)

- market-data-validator: Validates market data ingestion pipelines for correctness, timezone handling, corporate action adjustments, missing bar detection, and stale data protection. Use before any data pipeline change and before running backtests on new data. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- misra-reviewer: Reviews C or C++ code against MISRA C:2023 and MISRA C++:2023 guidelines. Flags Mandatory, Required, and Advisory violations, identifies deviation candidates, and prepares findings for formal deviation records. Use on any safety-critical C or C++ code before review or static analysis tool runs. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- npc-dialogue-designer: Designs and implements NPC dialogue systems for the LLM-NPC game. Knows the schema-as-contract principle, structured JSON output format, character constraint system, function-calling trust boundary, and token efficiency patterns. Use when adding a new NPC type, behavior, or modifying the dialogue schema. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- prompt-optimizer: Reviews and tightens NPC system prompts for token efficiency without losing character fidelity or schema compliance. Measures token count impact and validates that optimized prompts produce the same schema-compliant outputs. Use after any NPC prompt change and before shipping a new character. (Tools: Read, Write, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- pyqt6-block-builder: Builds new hardware block components for the Silmulator PyQt6 drag-and-drop GUI. Knows the block pattern, canvas integration, signal/slot connections, and visual conventions. Use when adding a new device type that needs a GUI representation on the canvas. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob)

- requirements-tracer: Checks bidirectional traceability between system requirements, HLR, LLR, code, and tests. Finds orphaned requirements, orphaned code, missing test coverage by requirement, and broken traceability chains. Core DO-178C compliance foundation. Use before any compliance review or DER interaction. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- reviewer: Routine pre-commit reviewer for bugs, security, and style (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- risk-reviewer: Reviews trading code for unintended orders, runaway position sizing, missing kill switches, and dangerous execution logic. The trading equivalent of a strict-reviewer. Use before any change to order management, position sizing, execution logic, or live trading infrastructure. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- scpi-implementer: Implements SCPI command handlers for new virtual devices in the Silmulator project. Knows the BaseDevice pattern, mandatory IEEE 488.2 commands, short-form aliasing, ErrorQueue behavior, and register conventions. Use when adding a new device class or extending an existing one's command set. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob)

- software-lifecycle-doc-reviewer: Reviews DO-178C software lifecycle plans (PSAC, SDP, SVP, SCMP, SQAP) for internal consistency, completeness, and coherence with each other before DER review. Plans are where compliance breaks first — this agent catches the "plan says X but we're doing Y" gaps before they become audit findings. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)
- strict-reviewer: Adversarial reviewer for milestone audits, releases, and high-stakes changes. Assumes code is wrong until proven right. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- tester: Writes and runs tests for new or modified code (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash)

- tool-qualification-prep: Prepares Tool Operational Requirements (TOR), qualification evidence structure, and TQL determination for DO-330 tool qualification. Use when a development or verification tool needs to be qualified for use in a DAL A-D software project. (Tools: Read, Write, Grep, Glob)

content.text:
You are running an overnight autonomous development session on this
repository. Use the overnight-coordinator agent to manage the full session.
You have full permission to read, write, commit, push, and open draft PRs.
You do NOT have permission to merge to main or close PRs after opening them.

## SETUP (run once at session start)

```bash
# 1. Ensure we are on main and up to date
git checkout main
git pull

# 2. Rebuild the knowledge graph so you navigate current code, not stale code
# (only if graphify is installed — skip silently if not)
graphify update . --force 2>/dev/null || echo "graphify not installed — skipping"

# 3. Check for a prior checkpoint (resume if interrupted)
cat .claude/memory/checkpoint.md 2>/dev/null || echo "No checkpoint — starting fresh"

# 4. Read tonight's issues
gh issue list --label "ready-for-ai" --json number,title,body,labels \
  --order created --limit 20
```

If a checkpoint exists and shows IN PROGRESS or FAILED stages, resume
from there rather than starting over.

Write the session start to .claude/memory/checkpoint.md:
```
# Checkpoint
Session started: [timestamp]
Goal: Work through all ready-for-ai issues
Status: IN PROGRESS
Issues to process: [list from gh output]
Issues completed: []
Issues failed: []
Issues skipped: []
```

---

## FOR EACH ISSUE (in number order, lowest first)

### A. READ AND ASSESS

```bash
gh issue view [N] --comments
```

Ask: Is this issue clear enough to attempt autonomously?

**Blockers that cause a SKIP:**
- Requires a design decision not documented in the issue
- Depends on another issue that isn't complete yet
- Requires credentials, API keys, or external resources not available
- Scope is too vague to produce a verifiable result

If blocked, label and move on — do NOT guess at intent:
```bash
gh issue edit [N] --add-label "needs-human" --remove-label "ready-for-ai"
gh issue comment [N] --body "Skipped overnight: [specific reason]. Please clarify before re-queuing."
```

### B. ORIENT

Invoke the git-historian agent:
"Use the git-historian agent to understand the code area this issue will touch."

This surfaces hot files, recent decisions, and things NOT to redo.
Read .claude/memory/history-brief.md after it completes.

### C. MARK IN PROGRESS

```bash
gh issue edit [N] --add-label "ai-in-progress" --remove-label "ready-for-ai"
gh issue comment [N] --body "Starting overnight implementation. Planning now."
```

### D. BRANCH

```bash
git checkout main
git checkout -b feature/issue-[N]
```

### E. PLAN

Use /plan-feature [concept from issue title] and wait for a plan.
Save the plan to .claude/plans/issue-[N].md

Do not implement until you have a written plan.

### F. IMPLEMENT

Use the appropriate specialist agents for this repo (see repo-specific
section below). Follow the plan. Write complete code — no placeholders.

If you hit a problem after 2 attempts on the same sticking point, SKIP
the issue and mark it ai-blocked. Do not spiral.

### G. TEST

Run the project's test suite. The exact commands are in the repo-specific
section below. Tests MUST pass before committing.

If tests fail after 2 fix attempts: skip, mark blocked, move on.
```bash
gh issue edit [N] --remove-label "ai-in-progress" --add-label "ai-blocked"
gh issue comment [N] --body "Blocked: tests failing after 2 attempts. [describe failure]. Needs human attention."
git checkout main
git branch -D feature/issue-[N]
```

### H. COMMIT AND PUSH

```bash
git add .
git commit -m "fix(#[N]): [issue title, shortened]"
git push origin feature/issue-[N]
```

### I. OPEN DRAFT PR

Generate the PR description using the /mr-description command, then:

```bash
gh pr create \
  --title "fix(#[N]): [issue title]" \
  --body "[output from /mr-description]" \
  --base main \
  --head feature/issue-[N] \
  --draft
```

Label the issue complete and close it with a reference to the PR:
```bash
gh issue edit [N] \
  --remove-label "ai-in-progress" \
  --add-label "ai-completed"
gh issue close [N] \
  --comment "Implemented. Draft PR open for review — see above."
```

### J. GENERATE LEARNING MATERIALS

**Identify the primary concept:**
Ask yourself: "What is the single most important technical concept a
developer would need to understand to maintain or extend this change?"

Guidelines:
- Choose the concept, not the feature name
  ("triple-channel SCPI addressing" not "E3631A support")
- Should be teachable in one lesson
- Should have testable recall in a drill
- Should introduce vocabulary worth learning

Then generate all three artifacts. In overnight/automated context:
- Generate the HTML files fully
- Skip in-chat interactive knowledge checks (no user present)
- Make the HTML content thorough — it is the only output
- Update PROGRESS.md with what was covered

```
/teach [concept]
```
This creates docs/learning/lessons/NNNN-[concept].html

```
/drill-me [concept]
```
This creates docs/learning/drills/NNNN-[concept].html

```
/terms [concept]
```
This creates docs/learning/vocab/NNNN-[concept].html
and updates docs/learning/GLOSSARY.md

Commit the learning materials on the same feature branch:
```bash
git add docs/learning/
git commit -m "docs(learning): add lesson, drill and vocab for [concept] (from issue #[N])"
git push origin feature/issue-[N]
```

### K. UPDATE CHECKPOINT

Append to .claude/memory/checkpoint.md:
```
Issue #[N]: [COMPLETED | FAILED | SKIPPED]
  Branch: feature/issue-[N]
  PR: #[PR number if opened]
  Concept taught: [concept]
  Learning files: lessons/NNNN-x.html, drills/NNNN-x.html, vocab/NNNN-x.html
  Notes: [anything notable]
```

Return to main: `git checkout main`

---

## END OF ALL ISSUES

### 1. Rebuild the learning index

```
/index
```

Commit:
```bash
git add docs/learning/index.html
git commit -m "docs(learning): rebuild index after overnight run $(date +%Y-%m-%d)"
git push origin main
```

### 2. Write the morning report

Write OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md to the repo root:

```markdown
# Overnight Build Report
Date: [date]
Session duration: [start] to [finish]
Issues attempted: [N]

## Summary
[2-3 sentences on what was accomplished overall]

## Completed ✅
| Issue | Title | Branch | PR | Concept Taught |
|-------|-------|--------|----|----------------|
| #N | [title] | feature/issue-N | #PR | [concept] |

## Failed ❌
| Issue | Title | Failure Reason |
|-------|-------|----------------|
| #N | [title] | [why — specific, actionable] |

## Skipped (needs human) ⏭
| Issue | Title | Reason |
|-------|-------|--------|
| #N | [title] | [what needs clarification] |

## Learning Materials Created
| Concept | Lesson | Drill | Vocab |
|---------|--------|-------|-------|
| [concept] | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

## Test Status
[overall pass/fail and any notable failures]

## Suggested First Move
[The single most useful thing to do when you open your laptop]

## Draft PRs Awaiting Review
[list with PR numbers and one-line description each]
```

Commit and push the report:
```bash
git add OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md .claude/memory/checkpoint.md
git commit -m "chore: overnight report $(date +%Y-%m-%d)"
git push origin main
```

---

## LEARNING CONCEPT SELECTION — GENERAL GUIDANCE

These guidelines apply to all repos unless overridden in a repo-specific
overnight-session command.

Choose a concept that:
- Is non-obvious (skip things any developer already knows)
- Will appear again in this codebase (worth learning for maintainability)
- Can be explained in one lesson without splitting into prerequisite lessons
- Has clear vocabulary (terms worth adding to the glossary)
- Produces useful recall questions in a drill

Avoid:
- Concepts named after specific model numbers or vendor names
  ("E3631A" is not a concept; "triple-channel PSU SCPI addressing" is)
- Concepts so generic they produce a useless lesson
  ("adding a class" — skip this)
- Concepts already well-covered in the existing lesson library
  (check docs/learning/PROGRESS.md first)

---

## FAILURE HANDLING POLICY

This policy applies to the entire session.

**Never stop the run because one issue failed.**
**Never silently skip — always label and comment.**
**Never attempt a risky or irreversible action without a prior commit.**

If at any point the session hits a situation that is genuinely ambiguous,
dangerous, or requires a human decision not covered by the issue:
1. Stop work on that issue
2. Label it needs-human
3. Leave a detailed comment explaining exactly what decision is needed
4. Move to the next issue

The goal is to maximize completed work, not to force through stuck issues.

---

## NOTE ON AUTOMATED LEARNING GENERATION

In a live session, /teach, /drill-me, and /terms end with in-chat
knowledge checks. In overnight autonomous mode, skip the interactive
questions and put that energy into making the HTML content more thorough
instead. The HTML is the deliverable — the in-chat conversation is not.

content.content:
1	# Plan: C++ Core — Oil-Volume Reader + ITCH Order-Book Perf Lab
2	Date: 2026-06-28
3	Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
4	Estimated complexity: XL (split into two shippable tracks below)
5	
6	## The Idea (one paragraph)
7	The repo today is a pure-Python crude-oil lead-lag research kit (`src/oil_alpha`,
8	Streamlit GUI in `app/dashboard.py`). Two GitHub tickets push it toward the
9	"systems / performance" side of HFT, in C++. **Issue #1** ("famous oil drum
10	investigation") wants the heavy compute for *reading the physical size of oil*
11	— aggregating EIA/FRED storage-volume and production series into clean,
12	fast-to-compute volume metrics — written in C++ and surfaced in the existing
13	GUI. **Issue #2** wants a C++ **Nasdaq TotalView-ITCH parser + order-book
14	engine**, then a measure→optimize→measure loop (perf stat, HdrHistogram tail
15	latencies, data-structure swaps) to drive down tick-to-trade latency, using
16	Claude to explain *why* each change got faster. Both tickets need the same new
17	foundation: a **CMake + pybind11 C++ build layer** added to the repo once and
18	shared by both. That shared foundation is Track 0.
19	
20	## Goal
21	A user can (a) compute oil storage/production "size" metrics from real EIA data
22	via a fast C++ core exposed to the Streamlit GUI, and (b) run a C++ binary that
23	parses real ITCH messages, rebuilds the L2/L3 book, and prints p50/p99/p99.9
24	tick-to-trade latency — then re-run it after an optimization and see the tail
25	shrink, with a written explanation of the cause.
26	
27	## Out of Scope (this version)
28	- FPGA / hardware acceleration (the "Level 2/3" follow-on is explicitly later).
29	- Live exchange connectivity or real order routing — replay/synthetic only.
30	- SIMD/branchless micro-optimization of ITCH parsing in the *first* pass
31	  (captured as a later issue once the baseline + harness exist).
32	- Rewriting the existing Python lead-lag analytics in C++ — only the new
33	  oil-volume compute is C++.
34	- Windows/macOS support for the perf harness (`perf`/HdrHistogram target Linux,
35	  which matches the dev environment).
36	
37	## Affected Areas
38	- New `cpp/` top-level tree (C++17):
39	  - `cpp/CMakeLists.txt` — root build; pybind11 + two targets (oil core lib,
40	    ITCH bench binary).
41	  - `cpp/oil_volume/` — `volume_metrics.{hpp,cpp}` (storage/production
42	    aggregation), `bindings.cpp` (pybind11 module `oil_volume_cpp`).
43	  - `cpp/itch/` — `itch_parser.{hpp,cpp}`, `order_book.{hpp,cpp}`,
44	    `signal.{hpp,cpp}`, `bench_main.cpp` (the tick-to-trade benchmark).
45	  - `cpp/common/` — `latency_histogram.hpp` (HdrHistogram wrapper),
46	    arena/preallocation helpers used later.
47	  - `cpp/third_party/` — pybind11 + HdrHistogram_c as submodules or
48	    `FetchContent`.
49	- `src/oil_alpha/data/sources.py` — add `fetch_eia()` for storage/production
50	  volume series (key already stubbed in `.env.example` as `EIA_API_KEY`).
51	- `src/oil_alpha/oil_volume.py` — thin Python wrapper that calls the
52	  `oil_volume_cpp` extension (with a pure-Python fallback if the ext isn't built).
53	- `app/dashboard.py` — new "Oil Size / Volume" panel.
54	- `scripts/perf_stat.sh` — wraps `perf stat` (cycles, instructions, IPC,
55	  cache-misses, branch-misses) around the ITCH bench.
56	- `requirements.txt` / `pyproject.toml` — add `pybind11`, build config.
57	- New: `cpp/README.md`, `docs/perf/` (where measure→optimize→measure write-ups land).
58	- `tests/test_oil_volume.py`, `cpp/tests/` (gtest or simple asserts).
59	
60	## Implementation Order
61	Each step is independently committable.
62	
63	**Track 0 — Shared C++ build foundation**
64	1. Add `cpp/CMakeLists.txt` + pybind11 via `FetchContent`; a trivial
65	   `oil_volume_cpp` module exposing `add(a,b)` that imports from Python. Wire
66	   `pyproject.toml` so `pip install -e .` builds it. Produces: a working
67	   C++→Python bridge proven by one passing test.
68	
69	**Track A — Oil-volume reader (Issue #1)**
70	2. `fetch_eia()` in `sources.py` — pull Cushing/storage + production volume
71	   series (paginated EIA v2), cached via existing `data/cache.py`, charged via
72	   existing `APIBudget`.
73	3. C++ `volume_metrics` — aggregation/rolling computations over the volume
74	   series (capacity utilization %, days-of-supply, fill-rate); pybind11-exposed.
75	4. `oil_volume.py` wrapper + Streamlit "Oil Size / Volume" panel rendering the
76	   metrics and a time series. Produces: GUI shows oil "size" from real data via
77	   the C++ core.
78	
79	**Track B — ITCH order-book perf lab (Issue #2)**
80	5. `itch_parser` — decode the TotalView-ITCH 5.0 message subset needed for the
81	   book (Add/Delete/Replace/Execute); fed by a downloaded Nasdaq sample file.
82	6. `order_book` — baseline **hash-map by price level** L2/L3 reconstruction;
83	   `signal` emits a trivial top-of-book signal. Correctness tested against a
84	   tiny hand-built message sequence.
85	7. `latency_histogram` + `bench_main` — measure per-message tick-to-trade
86	   latency, print p50/p99/p99.9; `scripts/perf_stat.sh` captures CPU counters.
87	   Produces: a baseline number + the full measurement loop.
88	8. First optimization commit: swap hash-map → **flat array indexed by price
89	   level**; re-run; record before/after in `docs/perf/01-flat-book.md` with
90	   Claude's explanation of the cache-miss drop. Produces: the "got faster + why"
91	   artifact the ticket asks for.
92	
93	## Acceptance Criteria
94	- [ ] `pip install -e .` builds the C++ extension; `import oil_volume_cpp` works.
95	- [ ] Given EIA storage data, the GUI "Oil Size / Volume" panel renders capacity
96	      utilization % and a volume time series computed by the C++ core.
97	- [ ] C++ oil metrics match a Python reference within 1e-9 (parity test).
98	- [ ] Given a Nasdaq ITCH sample file, `bench_main` reconstructs the book and
99	      prints p50/p99/p99.9 tick-to-trade latency without crashing.
100	- [ ] Order book reconstruction passes a unit test on a known message sequence
101	      (correct best bid/ask after Add/Execute/Delete).
102	- [ ] `scripts/perf_stat.sh` prints cycles, instructions, IPC, cache-misses,
103	      branch-misses for the bench run.
104	- [ ] After the flat-array swap, p99 latency drops vs. the hash-map baseline and
105	      `docs/perf/01-flat-book.md` documents the before/after + cause.
106	- [ ] Tests pass: `pytest` (Python) and `ctest`/`cpp/tests` (C++).
107	
108	## Edge Cases and Error Handling
109	| Situation | Expected behaviour |
110	|-----------|-------------------|

# Plan: C++ Core — Oil-Volume Reader + ITCH Order-Book Perf Lab
Date: 2026-06-28
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: XL (split into two shippable tracks below)

## The Idea (one paragraph)
The repo today is a pure-Python crude-oil lead-lag research kit (`src/oil_alpha`,
Streamlit GUI in `app/dashboard.py`). Two GitHub tickets push it toward the
"systems / performance" side of HFT, in C++. **Issue #1** ("famous oil drum
investigation") wants the heavy compute for *reading the physical size of oil*
— aggregating EIA/FRED storage-volume and production series into clean,
fast-to-compute volume metrics — written in C++ and surfaced in the existing
GUI. **Issue #2** wants a C++ **Nasdaq TotalView-ITCH parser + order-book
engine**, then a measure→optimize→measure loop (perf stat, HdrHistogram tail
latencies, data-structure swaps) to drive down tick-to-trade latency, using
Claude to explain *why* each change got faster. Both tickets need the same new
foundation: a **CMake + pybind11 C++ build layer** added to the repo once and
shared by both. That shared foundation is Track 0.

## Goal
A user can (a) compute oil storage/production "size" metrics from real EIA data
via a fast C++ core exposed to the Streamlit GUI, and (b) run a C++ binary that
parses real ITCH messages, rebuilds the L2/L3 book, and prints p50/p99/p99.9
tick-to-trade latency — then re-run it after an optimization and see the tail
shrink, with a written explanation of the cause.

## Out of Scope (this version)
- FPGA / hardware acceleration (the "Level 2/3" follow-on is explicitly later).
- Live exchange connectivity or real order routing — replay/synthetic only.
- SIMD/branchless micro-optimization of ITCH parsing in the *first* pass
  (captured as a later issue once the baseline + harness exist).
- Rewriting the existing Python lead-lag analytics in C++ — only the new
  oil-volume compute is C++.
- Windows/macOS support for the perf harness (`perf`/HdrHistogram target Linux,
  which matches the dev environment).

## Affected Areas
- New `cpp/` top-level tree (C++17):
  - `cpp/CMakeLists.txt` — root build; pybind11 + two targets (oil core lib,
    ITCH bench binary).
  - `cpp/oil_volume/` — `volume_metrics.{hpp,cpp}` (storage/production
    aggregation), `bindings.cpp` (pybind11 module `oil_volume_cpp`).
  - `cpp/itch/` — `itch_parser.{hpp,cpp}`, `order_book.{hpp,cpp}`,
    `signal.{hpp,cpp}`, `bench_main.cpp` (the tick-to-trade benchmark).
  - `cpp/common/` — `latency_histogram.hpp` (HdrHistogram wrapper),
    arena/preallocation helpers used later.
  - `cpp/third_party/` — pybind11 + HdrHistogram_c as submodules or
    `FetchContent`.
- `src/oil_alpha/data/sources.py` — add `fetch_eia()` for storage/production
  volume series (key already stubbed in `.env.example` as `EIA_API_KEY`).
- `src/oil_alpha/oil_volume.py` — thin Python wrapper that calls the
  `oil_volume_cpp` extension (with a pure-Python fallback if the ext isn't built).
- `app/dashboard.py` — new "Oil Size / Volume" panel.
- `scripts/perf_stat.sh` — wraps `perf stat` (cycles, instructions, IPC,
  cache-misses, branch-misses) around the ITCH bench.
- `requirements.txt` / `pyproject.toml` — add `pybind11`, build config.
- New: `cpp/README.md`, `docs/perf/` (where measure→optimize→measure write-ups land).
- `tests/test_oil_volume.py`, `cpp/tests/` (gtest or simple asserts).

## Implementation Order
Each step is independently committable.

**Track 0 — Shared C++ build foundation**
1. Add `cpp/CMakeLists.txt` + pybind11 via `FetchContent`; a trivial
   `oil_volume_cpp` module exposing `add(a,b)` that imports from Python. Wire
   `pyproject.toml` so `pip install -e .` builds it. Produces: a working
   C++→Python bridge proven by one passing test.

**Track A — Oil-volume reader (Issue #1)**
2. `fetch_eia()` in `sources.py` — pull Cushing/storage + production volume
   series (paginated EIA v2), cached via existing `data/cache.py`, charged via
   existing `APIBudget`.
3. C++ `volume_metrics` — aggregation/rolling computations over the volume
   series (capacity utilization %, days-of-supply, fill-rate); pybind11-exposed.
4. `oil_volume.py` wrapper + Streamlit "Oil Size / Volume" panel rendering the
   metrics and a time series. Produces: GUI shows oil "size" from real data via
   the C++ core.

**Track B — ITCH order-book perf lab (Issue #2)**
5. `itch_parser` — decode the TotalView-ITCH 5.0 message subset needed for the
   book (Add/Delete/Replace/Execute); fed by a downloaded Nasdaq sample file.
6. `order_book` — baseline **hash-map by price level** L2/L3 reconstruction;
   `signal` emits a trivial top-of-book signal. Correctness tested against a
   tiny hand-built message sequence.
7. `latency_histogram` + `bench_main` — measure per-message tick-to-trade
   latency, print p50/p99/p99.9; `scripts/perf_stat.sh` captures CPU counters.
   Produces: a baseline number + the full measurement loop.
8. First optimization commit: swap hash-map → **flat array indexed by price
   level**; re-run; record before/after in `docs/perf/01-flat-book.md` with
   Claude's explanation of the cache-miss drop. Produces: the "got faster + why"
   artifact the ticket asks for.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `pip install -e .` builds the C++ extension; `import oil_volume_cpp` works.
- [ ] Given EIA storage data, the GUI "Oil Size / Volume" panel renders capacity
      utilization % and a volume time series computed by the C++ core.
- [ ] C++ oil metrics match a Python reference within 1e-9 (parity test).
- [ ] Given a Nasdaq ITCH sample file, `bench_main` reconstructs the book and
      prints p50/p99/p99.9 tick-to-trade latency without crashing.
- [ ] Order book reconstruction passes a unit test on a known message sequence
      (correct best bid/ask after Add/Execute/Delete).
- [ ] `scripts/perf_stat.sh` prints cycles, instructions, IPC, cache-misses,
      branch-misses for the bench run.
- [ ] After the flat-array swap, p99 latency drops vs. the hash-map baseline and
      `docs/perf/01-flat-book.md` documents the before/after + cause.
- [ ] Tests pass: `pytest` (Python) and `ctest`/`cpp/tests` (C++).

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| C++ extension not built | `oil_volume.py` falls back to a pure-Python implementation and the GUI shows a "running unoptimized" notice |
| `EIA_API_KEY` missing | `fetch_eia()` raises a clear, actionable error; GUI panel shows setup hint (consistent with existing keyless-FRED pattern) |
| ITCH file truncated / unknown message type | Parser skips unknown types, logs a count, never reads past buffer end |
| Malformed book op (delete missing order) | Engine ignores + increments an error counter, does not corrupt the book |
| `perf` not permitted (`perf_event_paranoid`) | Script detects non-zero exit, prints the sysctl fix, still emits HdrHistogram latencies (which don't need perf) |
| Negative/zero storage values in EIA series | Filtered like the existing `clean.py` positive-price guard |

## Open Questions
- **Binding tool**: plan assumes **pybind11 + CMake (FetchContent)**. If you'd
  rather use `nanobind` or `scikit-build-core`, flag before Track 0.
- **ITCH sample source**: assumes a downloaded Nasdaq TotalView-ITCH 5.0 sample
  (e.g. the public `emi.nasdaq.com` sample). Confirm you can obtain one, or we
  start Track B on a synthetic ITCH generator and swap in the real file later.
- **C++ test framework**: GoogleTest vs. a header-only assert harness — default
  to GoogleTest via FetchContent unless you want zero extra deps.

## Suggested GitHub Issues
For `/plan-github`:
1. **C++ build foundation (CMake + pybind11)** — Track 0; `cpp/` tree, trivial
   bound module, `pip install -e .` builds it, one passing parity test.
2. **EIA oil-volume data source + C++ metrics core** — Track A steps 2–3;
   `fetch_eia()`, `volume_metrics`, parity test.
3. **Oil Size / Volume GUI panel** — Track A step 4; Streamlit panel + Python
   fallback wrapper.
4. **ITCH parser + baseline (hash-map) order book** — Track B steps 5–6;
   correctness test on a known message sequence.
5. **Tick-to-trade latency harness (HdrHistogram + perf stat)** — Track B step 7;
   p50/p99/p99.9 + CPU-counter script.
6. **Optimization #1: flat-array book + perf write-up** — Track B step 8;
   before/after doc in `docs/perf/`.

"""Price/series fetchers for the free no-token stack (paper Part 1, Tier A).

Each fetcher returns a tidy DataFrame indexed by date with a ``close`` column
(and ``open/high/low/volume`` where available). Network libraries are imported
lazily so the rest of the package (and the test suite) imports without them.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import urllib.request

import pandas as pd

from oil_alpha.config import FRED_SERIES, STOOQ_SUFFIX, SYMBOLS
from oil_alpha.data import cache
from oil_alpha.data.budget import APIBudget

_OHLCV = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"]


def _from_cache_or(
    kind: str,
    symbol: str,
    start: str,
    end: str,
    fetch,
    *,
    budget: APIBudget,
    source: str,
    use_cache: bool,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    if use_cache:
        cached = cache.load(kind, symbol, start, end)
        if cached is not None and not cached.empty:
            return cached
    df = fetch()
    budget.charge(source)
    if use_cache and not df.empty:
        cache.save(df, kind, symbol, start, end)
    return df


def fetch_yf(
    symbol: str,
    start: str,
    end: str,
    *,
    budget: APIBudget,
    use_cache: bool = True,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Daily OHLCV from Yahoo via yfinance.

    ``auto_adjust=True`` is passed *explicitly* because the yfinance default
    flipped from False to True in 2025 (paper Part 1, "Critical 2025 change"):
    pinning it removes the ambiguity older tutorials assume.
    """

    def _fetch() -> pd.DataFrame:
        import yfinance as yf

        raw = yf.download(
            symbol,
            start=start,
            end=end,
            auto_adjust=True,      # explicit: see docstring
            progress=False,
            multi_level_index=False,
        )
        if raw is None or raw.empty:
            return pd.DataFrame(columns=_OHLCV)
        raw = raw.rename(columns=str.lower)
        keep = [c for c in _OHLCV if c in raw.columns]
        out = raw[keep].copy()
        out.index = pd.to_datetime(out.index).tz_localize(None)
        out.index.name = "date"
        return out

    return _from_cache_or(

    start: str,
    end: str,
    fetch,
    *,
    budget: APIBudget,
    source: str,
    use_cache: bool,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    if use_cache:
        cached = cache.load(kind, symbol, start, end)
        if cached is not None and not cached.empty:

"""Streamlit dashboard for the CL-vs-XLE lead-lag study.

Run:  ``streamlit run app/dashboard.py``

Shows live pipeline *progress*, a *results* panel (CCF curve, Granger p-values,
cointegration verdict, rolling corr/beta), and a *costs* panel with the three
flavours the user asked for: API free-tier budget, hypothetical transaction
cost, and per-stage compute time.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys

# Make ``src`` importable when run via ``streamlit run app/dashboard.py``.
_SRC = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "src")
if _SRC not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(_SRC))

import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
import plotly.graph_objects as go  # noqa: E402
import streamlit as st  # noqa: E402

from oil_alpha.config import DEFAULT_START, LAG, LEAD, SYMBOLS, RunConfig, default_end  # noqa: E402
from oil_alpha.pipeline import ProgressEvent, run_pipeline  # noqa: E402

st.set_page_config(page_title="Crude-Oil Lead-Lag Lab", layout="wide")
st.title("🛢️ Crude-Oil Lead-Lag Lab")
st.caption(
    f"Does **{SYMBOLS[LEAD]} (WTI futures)** lead **{SYMBOLS[LAG]} (energy ETF)**? "
    "Daily study per the crude-oil research paper, Stages 1-3."
)

# --- Sidebar: run controls ---------------------------------------------------
with st.sidebar:
    st.header("Run settings")
    start = st.text_input("Start date", DEFAULT_START)
    end = st.text_input("End date", default_end())
    return_kind = st.radio("Return type", ["log", "simple"], horizontal=True)
    max_lag = st.slider("Max lag (trading days)", 1, 30, 10)
    rolling_window = st.slider("Rolling window", 20, 120, 60, step=10)
    drop_roll_days = st.checkbox("Drop CL=F roll-day jumps", value=True)
    use_cache = st.checkbox("Use local cache", value=True)
    turnover = st.number_input("Hypothetical turnover / yr", 1.0, 1000.0, 252.0, step=10.0)
    run = st.button("▶ Run pipeline", type="primary", use_container_width=True)
    st.markdown(
        "<small>yfinance + FRED need no API key. Negative-price (Apr-2020) and "
        "roll-day traps are handled automatically.</small>",
        unsafe_allow_html=True,
    )


def _ccf_figure(ll) -> go.Figure:
    fig = go.Figure()
    fig.add_bar(x=ll.lags, y=ll.ccf, name="CCF")
    fig.add_vline(x=ll.peak_lag, line_dash="dash", line_color="crimson")
    fig.add_annotation(
        x=ll.peak_lag, y=ll.peak_corr,
        text=f"peak lag {ll.peak_lag}", showarrow=True, arrowhead=2,
    )
    fig.update_layout(
        title=f"Cross-correlation  ρ(k)=corr({ll.x_name}ₜ, {ll.y_name}ₜ₊ₖ)   (k>0 ⇒ {ll.x_name} leads)",
        xaxis_title="lag k (days)", yaxis_title="correlation", height=340,
        margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=50, b=10),
    )
    return fig


def _line(series: pd.Series, title: str, yaxis: str) -> go.Figure:
    fig = go.Figure()
    fig.add_scatter(x=series.index, y=series.to_numpy(), mode="lines")
    fig.update_layout(title=title, yaxis_title=yaxis, height=300, margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=40, b=10))
    return fig


def _render_results(result) -> None:
    ll = result.leadlag
    st.subheader("Results")

    c1, c2, c3 = st.columns(3)
    leader = "CL (futures)" if ll.x_leads else ("XLE" if ll.peak_lag < 0 else "contemporaneous")
    c1.metric("Lead-lag leader", leader, f"peak lag {ll.peak_lag}")
    if result.granger:
        g = result.granger["x->y"]
        c2.metric(f"Granger {SYMBOLS[LEAD]}→{SYMBOLS[LAG]}", f"p={g.p_value:.3f}",
                  "significant" if g.significant else "n.s.")
    if result.spot_check:
        c3.metric("CL=F vs FRED spot", f"{result.spot_check['median_abs_pct']:.1f}%",
                  f"{result.spot_check['common_days']} common days")

    st.plotly_chart(_ccf_figure(ll), use_container_width=True)

    gc, cc = st.columns(2)
    with gc:
        st.markdown("**Granger causality (both directions)**")
        if result.granger:
            rows = [
                {"direction": g.direction, "best lag": g.best_lag,
                 "p-value": round(g.p_value, 4), "significant": g.significant}
                for g in result.granger.values()
            ]
            st.dataframe(pd.DataFrame(rows), hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)
            st.caption("Granger = predictive precedence, not true causation (paper Part 2.3).")
    with cc:
        st.markdown("**Cointegration (price levels)**")
        if result.eg_coint:
            st.write("•", result.eg_coint.verdict)
        if result.johansen_coint:
            st.write("•", result.johansen_coint.verdict)

    rc, rb = st.columns(2)
    if result.rolling_corr is not None and not result.rolling_corr.empty:
        rc.plotly_chart(
            _line(result.rolling_corr, f"Rolling correlation ({SYMBOLS[LEAD]} vs {SYMBOLS[LAG]})", "corr"),
            use_container_width=True,
        )
    if result.rolling_beta is not None and not result.rolling_beta.empty:
        rb.plotly_chart(
            _line(result.rolling_beta, f"Rolling β of {SYMBOLS[LAG]} to oil", "beta"),
            use_container_width=True,
        )

    if result.warnings:
        for w in result.warnings:
            st.warning(w)


def _render_costs(result) -> None:
    st.subheader("Projected costs")
    a, b, c = st.tabs(["① API free-tier budget", "② Transaction cost", "③ Compute / time"])

    with a:
        rows = result.budget.as_rows()
        if rows:
            df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
            st.dataframe(df, hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)
            for r in rows:
                if r["cap"] is not None:
                    st.progress(min(1.0, r["fraction"] or 0.0),
                                text=f"{r['source']}: {r['used']}/{r['cap']} used")
        st.caption(f"Total requests this run: {result.budget.total_requests()} "
                   "(yfinance/FRED have no hard cap; capped sources shown with bars).")

    with b:
        if result.cost_estimates:
            df = pd.DataFrame([
                {"asset": SYMBOLS.get(c.asset_key, c.asset_key),
                 "round-trip (bp)": round(c.round_trip_bp, 2),
                 "turnover/yr": c.turnover_per_year,
                 "annual drag (bp)": round(c.annual_drag_bp, 1),
                 "annual drag (%)": round(c.annual_drag_pct, 2)}
                for c in result.cost_estimates
            ])
            st.dataframe(df, hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)
        st.caption("Illustrative half-spread + commission assumptions (config.COST_MODEL), "
                   "not calibrated to live quotes.")

    with c:
        if result.metrics:
            st.dataframe(pd.DataFrame(result.metrics.as_rows()), hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)
            st.metric("Total compute time", f"{result.metrics.total_seconds:.2f} s")


def _run(cfg: RunConfig) -> None:
    progress = st.progress(0.0, text="starting…")
    with st.status("Running pipeline…", expanded=True) as status:
        final = None
        for event in run_pipeline(cfg):
            progress.progress(event.pct, text=f"{event.stage} — {event.message}")
            icon = {"ok": "✅", "warn": "⚠️", "error": "❌", "done": "🏁"}.get(event.status, "•")
            if event.status != "start":
                st.write(f"{icon} **{event.stage}** — {event.message}")
            if event.stage == "done":
                final = event.payload
        status.update(label="Pipeline complete", state="complete")
    st.session_state["result"] = final


if run:
    cfg = RunConfig(
        start=start, end=end, return_kind=return_kind, max_lag=max_lag,
        rolling_window=rolling_window, drop_roll_days=drop_roll_days,
        use_cache=use_cache, turnover_per_year=turnover,
    )
    _run(cfg)

result = st.session_state.get("result")
if result is not None and result.leadlag is not None:
    _render_results(result)
    st.divider()
    _render_costs(result)
elif result is not None:
    st.error("Pipeline aborted before producing results. Check warnings above / network access.")
else:
    st.info("Set your window in the sidebar and click **▶ Run pipeline** to begin.")

    a, b, c = st.tabs(["① API free-tier budget", "② Transaction cost", "③ Compute / time"])

    with a:
        rows = result.budget.as_rows()
        if rows:
            df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
            st.dataframe(df, hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)
            for r in rows:
                if r["cap"] is not None:
                    st.progress(min(1.0, r["fraction"] or 0.0),
                                text=f"{r['source']}: {r['used']}/{r['cap']} used")
        st.caption(f"Total requests this run: {result.budget.total_requests()} "
                   "(yfinance/FRED have no hard cap; capped sources shown with bars).")

    with b:
        if result.cost_estimates:
            df = pd.DataFrame([
                {"asset": SYMBOLS.get(c.asset_key, c.asset_key),
                 "round-trip (bp)": round(c.round_trip_bp, 2),
                 "turnover/yr": c.turnover_per_year,
                 "annual drag (bp)": round(c.annual_drag_bp, 1),
                 "annual drag (%)": round(c.annual_drag_pct, 2)}
                for c in result.cost_estimates
            ])
            st.dataframe(df, hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)
        st.caption("Illustrative half-spread + commission assumptions (config.COST_MODEL), "
                   "not calibrated to live quotes.")

    with c:
        if result.metrics:
            st.dataframe(pd.DataFrame(result.metrics.as_rows()), hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)
            st.metric("Total compute time", f"{result.metrics.total_seconds:.2f} s")


def _run(cfg: RunConfig) -> None:
    progress = st.progress(0.0, text="starting…")
    with st.status("Running pipeline…", expanded=True) as status:
        final = None
        for event in run_pipeline(cfg):
            progress.progress(event.pct, text=f"{event.stage} — {event.message}")
            icon = {"ok": "✅", "warn": "⚠️", "error": "❌", "done": "🏁"}.get(event.status, "•")
            if event.status != "start":
                st.write(f"{icon} **{event.stage}** — {event.message}")
            if event.stage == "done":
                final = event.payload
        status.update(label="Pipeline complete", state="complete")
    st.session_state["result"] = final


if run:
    cfg = RunConfig(
        start=start, end=end, return_kind=return_kind, max_lag=max_lag,
        rolling_window=rolling_window, drop_roll_days=drop_roll_days,
        use_cache=use_cache, turnover_per_year=turnover,
    )
    _run(cfg)

result = st.session_state.get("result")
if result is not None and result.leadlag is not None:
    _render_results(result)
    st.divider()
    _render_costs(result)
elif result is not None:
    st.error("Pipeline aborted before producing results. Check warnings above / network access.")
else:
    st.info("Set your window in the sidebar and click **▶ Run pipeline** to begin.")

pip install -e .

- CMake ≥ 3.21  
- C++17-capable compiler (GCC 10+, Clang 13+)
- Python ≥ 3.10

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the C++ extension (oil_volume_cpp) and place the .so in src/oil_alpha/.
# This script works around environments where the system Python lacks dev headers.
# Usage: ./scripts/build_cpp.sh [python_executable]
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
BUILD_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/_build"

# Pick a Python that has dev headers.
PYTHON="${1:-}"
if [ -z "$PYTHON" ]; then
    # Prefer a uv-managed Python (has bundled headers).
    if command -v uv &>/dev/null; then
        PYTHON=$(uv python find 3.11 2>/dev/null || uv python find 3.12 2>/dev/null || true)
    fi
fi
PYTHON="${PYTHON:-python3}"

echo "Using Python: $PYTHON ($($PYTHON --version 2>&1))"

# Check Python headers are present.
INCLUDE_DIR=$($PYTHON -c "import sysconfig; print(sysconfig.get_path('include'))")
if [ ! -f "$INCLUDE_DIR/Python.h" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Python.h not found at $INCLUDE_DIR"
    echo "Install python3-dev (apt) or use a uv-managed Python: uv python install 3.11"
    exit 1
fi

# Locate pybind11 cmake config from pip-installed package.
PYBIND11_CMAKE=$($PYTHON -c "import pybind11; print(pybind11.get_cmake_dir())" 2>/dev/null || true)

CMAKE_EXTRA_ARGS=()
if [ -n "$PYBIND11_CMAKE" ]; then
    CMAKE_EXTRA_ARGS+=("-Dpybind11_DIR=$PYBIND11_CMAKE")
fi

mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR"
cmake -S "$REPO_ROOT" -B "$BUILD_DIR" \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DPython3_EXECUTABLE="$PYTHON" \
    -DCMAKE_LIBRARY_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY="$REPO_ROOT/src/oil_alpha" \
    "${CMAKE_EXTRA_ARGS[@]}"

cmake --build "$BUILD_DIR" --parallel "$(nproc)"

echo ""
echo "Extension built. Verify with:"
echo "  PYTHONPATH=src $PYTHON -c 'import oil_volume_cpp; print(oil_volume_cpp.rolling_mean([1,2,3,4,5], 3))'"

(Part 1, bottom line): yfinance for CL=F/XLE/USO/XOM/CVX cross-checked against

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as _dt
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

    "energy_etf": "XLE",  # Energy Select Sector SPDR
    "oil_etf": "USO",     # United States Oil Fund (positive across Apr-2020)
    "xom": "XOM",
    "cvx": "CVX",
}

    "wti_spot": "DCOILWTICO",

class AssetCost:
    """Round-trip transaction-cost assumptions for a tradeable asset, in basis points."""

    half_spread_bp: float
    commission_bp: float

        # Cross the spread twice (in + out) and pay commission twice.

"""Price/series fetchers for the free no-token stack (paper Part 1, Tier A).

Each fetcher returns a tidy DataFrame indexed by date with a ``close`` column
(and ``open/high/low/volume`` where available). Network libraries are imported
lazily so the rest of the package (and the test suite) imports without them.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

"""Price/series fetchers for the free no-token stack (paper Part 1, Tier A).

Each fetcher returns a tidy DataFrame indexed by date with a ``close`` column
(and ``open/high/low/volume`` where available). Network libraries are imported
lazily so the rest of the package (and the test suite) imports without them.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import urllib.request

import pandas as pd

from oil_alpha.config import FRED_SERIES, STOOQ_SUFFIX, SYMBOLS
from oil_alpha.data import cache
from oil_alpha.data.budget import APIBudget

_OHLCV = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"]


def _from_cache_or(
    kind: str,
    symbol: str,
    start: str,
    end: str,
    fetch,
    *,
    budget: APIBudget,
    source: str,
    use_cache: bool,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    if use_cache:
        cached = cache.load(kind, symbol, start, end)
        if cached is not None and not cached.empty:
            return cached
    df = fetch()
    budget.charge(source)
    if use_cache and not df.empty:
        cache.save(df, kind, symbol, start, end)
    return df


def fetch_yf(
    symbol: str,
    start: str,
    end: str,
    *,
    budget: APIBudget,
    use_cache: bool = True,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Daily OHLCV from Yahoo via yfinance.

    ``auto_adjust=True`` is passed *explicitly* because the yfinance default
    flipped from False to True in 2025 (paper Part 1, "Critical 2025 change"):
    pinning it removes the ambiguity older tutorials assume.
    """

    def _fetch() -> pd.DataFrame:
        import yfinance as yf

        raw = yf.download(
            symbol,
            start=start,
            end=end,
            auto_adjust=True,      # explicit: see docstring
            progress=False,
            multi_level_index=False,
        )
        if raw is None or raw.empty:
            return pd.DataFrame(columns=_OHLCV)
        raw = raw.rename(columns=str.lower)
        keep = [c for c in _OHLCV if c in raw.columns]
        out = raw[keep].copy()
        out.index = pd.to_datetime(out.index).tz_localize(None)
        out.index.name = "date"
        return out

    return _from_cache_or(
        "yf", symbol, start, end, _fetch, budget=budget, source="yfinance", use_cache=use_cache
    )


def fetch_fred(
    series: str,
    start: str,
    end: str,
    *,
    budget: APIBudget,
    use_cache: bool = True,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Daily series from FRED via the keyless CSV endpoint (no token needed).

    e.g. ``DCOILWTICO`` = WTI spot, Cushing OK, $/bbl. Returns a single
    ``close`` column for a uniform interface with the price fetchers.
    """

    def _fetch() -> pd.DataFrame:
        url = (
            "https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv"
            f"?id={series}&cosd={start}&coed={end}"
        )
        with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=30) as resp:  # noqa: S310 (trusted host)
            payload = resp.read().decode("utf-8")
        df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(payload))
        # FRED CSV: first column is the date; second is the series. Missing days are ".".
        date_col, value_col = df.columns[0], df.columns[1]
        df[value_col] = pd.to_numeric(df[value_col], errors="coerce")
        df = df.dropna(subset=[value_col])
        out = pd.DataFrame({"close": df[value_col].to_numpy()})
        out.index = pd.to_datetime(df[date_col]).to_numpy()
        out.index.name = "date"
        return out

    return _from_cache_or(
        "fred", series, start, end, _fetch, budget=budget, source="fred", use_cache=use_cache
    )


def fetch_stooq(
    symbol: str,
    start: str,
    end: str,
    *,
    budget: APIBudget,
    use_cache: bool = True,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Equities/ETF EOD from Stooq via pandas-datareader (fallback only).

    Append the ``.US`` suffix for US tickers. Do NOT use this for crude futures
    (e.g. ``CL.F``) -- that path has been broken via the Python API since ~2021
    (paper Part 1, Stooq limitations).
    """

    def _fetch() -> pd.DataFrame:
        from pandas_datareader import data as web

        ticker = symbol if "." in symbol else f"{symbol}{STOOQ_SUFFIX}"
        raw = web.DataReader(ticker, "stooq", start=start, end=end)
        if raw is None or raw.empty:
            return pd.DataFrame(columns=_OHLCV)
        raw = raw.rename(columns=str.lower).sort_index()
        keep = [c for c in _OHLCV if c in raw.columns]
        out = raw[keep].copy()
        out.index = pd.to_datetime(out.index).tz_localize(None)
        out.index.name = "date"
        return out

    return _from_cache_or(
        "stooq", symbol, start, end, _fetch, budget=budget, source="stooq", use_cache=use_cache
    )


def fetch_prices(
    keys: list[str],
    start: str,
    end: str,
    *,
    budget: APIBudget,
    use_cache: bool = True,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Fetch a set of config symbol *keys* via yfinance into one close-price frame.

    Columns are the config keys (e.g. ``wti_fut``, ``energy_etf``), not tickers,
    so downstream code is symbol-agnostic.
    """
    closes: dict[str, pd.Series] = {}
    for key in keys:
        ticker = SYMBOLS[key]
        df = fetch_yf(ticker, start, end, budget=budget, use_cache=use_cache)
        if not df.empty and "close" in df:
            closes[key] = df["close"].rename(key)
    if not closes:
        return pd.DataFrame()
    return pd.concat(closes.values(), axis=1)


def fetch_wti_spot(
    start: str,
    end: str,
    *,
    budget: APIBudget,
    use_cache: bool = True,
) -> pd.Series:
    """FRED DCOILWTICO spot close, for cross-checking CL=F (paper Stage 1 threshold)."""
    df = fetch_fred(FRED_SERIES["wti_spot"], start, end, budget=budget, use_cache=use_cache)
    return df["close"].rename("wti_spot") if not df.empty else pd.Series(dtype=float)

def fetch_eia(
    series_id: str,
    start: str,
    end: str,
    *,
    budget: APIBudget,
    use_cache: bool = True,
    api_key: str | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Fetch a single EIA v2 series and return a tidy dated DataFrame with a ``value`` column.

    Requires ``EIA_API_KEY`` in the environment (or pass ``api_key`` explicitly).
    Uses paginated EIA v2 ``/seriesid/`` endpoint (max 5000 rows/page).
    Non-positive values are filtered like the existing positive-price guard in clean.py.
    Results are cached via ``data/cache.py`` — a second call with the same window
    costs zero new API requests.

    Raises ``EnvironmentError`` if no key is found (consistent with the keyless-FRED pattern:
    clear, actionable error message).
    """
    key = api_key or os.environ.get("EIA_API_KEY", "")
    if not key:
        raise EnvironmentError(
            "EIA_API_KEY is not set. Add it to your .env file or pass api_key=. "
            "Register for a free key at https://www.eia.gov/opendata/register.php"
        )

    def _fetch() -> pd.DataFrame:
        rows: list[dict] = []
        offset = 0
        page_size = 5000
        while True:
            params = urllib.parse.urlencode({
                "api_key": key,
                "start": start,
                "end": end,
                "sort[0][column]": "period",
                "sort[0][direction]": "asc",
                "offset": offset,
                "length": page_size,
            })
            url = f"https://api.eia.gov/v2/seriesid/{series_id}?{params}"
            with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=30) as resp:  # noqa: S310
                payload = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))

            data = payload.get("response", {}).get("data", [])
            if not data:
                break
            rows.extend(data)
            if len(data) < page_size:
                break
            offset += page_size

        if not rows:
            return pd.DataFrame(columns=["value"])

        df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
        # EIA v2 uses "period" for the date and "value" for the observation.
        df["value"] = pd.to_numeric(df["value"], errors="coerce")
        df = df[df["value"] > 0].copy()   # filter non-positive like clean.py guard
        df = df.dropna(subset=["value"])
        out = pd.DataFrame({"value": df["value"].to_numpy()})
        out.index = pd.to_datetime(df["period"]).to_numpy()
        out.index.name = "date"
        out = out.sort_index()
        return out

    return _from_cache_or(
        "eia", series_id, start, end, _fetch, budget=budget, source="eia", use_cache=use_cache
    )

"""Tests for oil-volume metrics: C++ parity + fetch_eia() caching behaviour."""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
import os
import pytest


# ─── Helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def cpp():
    try:
        import oil_volume_cpp
        return oil_volume_cpp
    except ImportError:
        pytest.skip("oil_volume_cpp not built — run ./scripts/build_cpp.sh")


def _py_capacity_utilization(storage_kb, capacity_kb):
    return [v / capacity_kb * 100.0 for v in storage_kb]


def _py_days_of_supply(storage_kb, production_kbd):
    out = []
    for s, p in zip(storage_kb, production_kbd):
        out.append(float("nan") if p <= 0 else s / p)
    return out


def _py_fill_rate(storage_kb):
    out = [float("nan")]
    for i in range(1, len(storage_kb)):
        out.append(storage_kb[i] - storage_kb[i - 1])
    return out


def _close(a, b, tol=1e-9):
    if math.isnan(a) and math.isnan(b):
        return True
    if math.isnan(a) or math.isnan(b):
        return False
    return abs(a - b) < tol


# ─── capacity_utilization ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_capacity_utilization_parity(cpp):
    storage = [30000.0, 45000.0, 60000.0, 75000.0]
    cap = 76000.0
    got = cpp.capacity_utilization(storage, cap)
    expected = _py_capacity_utilization(storage, cap)
    assert all(_close(g, e) for g, e in zip(got, expected))


def test_capacity_utilization_invalid_capacity(cpp):
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        cpp.capacity_utilization([1.0, 2.0], 0.0)


# ─── days_of_supply ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_days_of_supply_parity(cpp):
    storage = [400000.0, 450000.0, 350000.0, 500000.0]
    prod = [12000.0, 12500.0, 11800.0, 12200.0]
    got = cpp.days_of_supply(storage, prod)
    expected = _py_days_of_supply(storage, prod)
    assert all(_close(g, e) for g, e in zip(got, expected))


def test_days_of_supply_zero_production_gives_nan(cpp):
    got = cpp.days_of_supply([100.0, 200.0], [0.0, 10.0])
    assert math.isnan(got[0])
    assert not math.isnan(got[1])


def test_days_of_supply_length_mismatch(cpp):
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        cpp.days_of_supply([1.0, 2.0], [1.0])


# ─── fill_rate ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_fill_rate_parity(cpp):
    storage = [300.0, 350.0, 330.0, 380.0]
    got = cpp.fill_rate(storage)
    expected = _py_fill_rate(storage)
    assert math.isnan(got[0])
    assert all(_close(g, e) for g, e in zip(got[1:], expected[1:]))


def test_fill_rate_single_element(cpp):
    got = cpp.fill_rate([500.0])
    assert len(got) == 1
    assert math.isnan(got[0])


# ─── fetch_eia (unit / caching) ───────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_fetch_eia_raises_without_key():
    from oil_alpha.data.sources import fetch_eia
    from oil_alpha.data.budget import APIBudget

    env_backup = os.environ.pop("EIA_API_KEY", None)
    try:
        with pytest.raises(EnvironmentError, match="EIA_API_KEY"):
            fetch_eia("PET.WCSSTUS1.W", "2023-01-01", "2023-12-31", budget=APIBudget())
    finally:
        if env_backup is not None:
            os.environ["EIA_API_KEY"] = env_backup


def test_fetch_eia_caches_on_second_call(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Second call must return the same data without charging the budget again."""
    import pandas as pd
    from oil_alpha.data.sources import fetch_eia
    from oil_alpha.data.budget import APIBudget
    from oil_alpha.data import cache

    # Prepopulate a fake cached frame so no real network call is made.
    fake = pd.DataFrame(
        {"value": [350000.0, 355000.0, 360000.0]},
        index=pd.to_datetime(["2023-01-06", "2023-01-13", "2023-01-20"]),
    )
    fake.index.name = "date"

    monkeypatch.setenv("EIA_API_KEY", "test-key")

    # Write to cache using the real cache key so fetch_eia finds it.
    cache.save(fake, "eia", "PET.WCSSTUS1.W", "2023-01-01", "2023-01-31",
               cache_dir=str(tmp_path))

    budget = APIBudget()
    monkeypatch.setattr(cache, "load", lambda *a, cache_dir=None: (
        cache.load(*a, cache_dir=str(tmp_path))
    ))
    monkeypatch.setattr(cache, "save", lambda *a, **kw: None)

    result = fetch_eia(
        "PET.WCSSTUS1.W", "2023-01-01", "2023-01-31",
        budget=budget, use_cache=True, api_key="test-key",
    )

    # Cache hit: result is the fake data; budget should show 0 eia charges.
    eia_usage = budget.usage.get("eia")
    assert eia_usage is None or eia_usage.used == 0
    assert not result.empty
    assert "value" in result.columns

"""Tests for oil-volume metrics: C++ parity + fetch_eia() caching behaviour."""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
import os
import pytest


# ─── Helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def cpp():
    try:
        import oil_volume_cpp
        return oil_volume_cpp
    except ImportError:
        pytest.skip("oil_volume_cpp not built — run ./scripts/build_cpp.sh")


def _py_capacity_utilization(storage_kb, capacity_kb):
    return [v / capacity_kb * 100.0 for v in storage_kb]


def _py_days_of_supply(storage_kb, production_kbd):
    out = []
    for s, p in zip(storage_kb, production_kbd):
        out.append(float("nan") if p <= 0 else s / p)
    return out


def _py_fill_rate(storage_kb):
    out = [float("nan")]
    for i in range(1, len(storage_kb)):
        out.append(storage_kb[i] - storage_kb[i - 1])
    return out


def _close(a, b, tol=1e-9):
    if math.isnan(a) and math.isnan(b):
        return True
    if math.isnan(a) or math.isnan(b):
        return False
    return abs(a - b) < tol


# ─── capacity_utilization ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_capacity_utilization_parity(cpp):
    storage = [30000.0, 45000.0, 60000.0, 75000.0]
    cap = 76000.0
    got = cpp.capacity_utilization(storage, cap)
    expected = _py_capacity_utilization(storage, cap)
    assert all(_close(g, e) for g, e in zip(got, expected))


def test_capacity_utilization_invalid_capacity(cpp):
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        cpp.capacity_utilization([1.0, 2.0], 0.0)


# ─── days_of_supply ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_days_of_supply_parity(cpp):
    storage = [400000.0, 450000.0, 350000.0, 500000.0]
    prod = [12000.0, 12500.0, 11800.0, 12200.0]
    got = cpp.days_of_supply(storage, prod)
    expected = _py_days_of_supply(storage, prod)
    assert all(_close(g, e) for g, e in zip(got, expected))


def test_days_of_supply_zero_production_gives_nan(cpp):
    got = cpp.days_of_supply([100.0, 200.0], [0.0, 10.0])
    assert math.isnan(got[0])
    assert not math.isnan(got[1])


def test_days_of_supply_length_mismatch(cpp):
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        cpp.days_of_supply([1.0, 2.0], [1.0])


# ─── fill_rate ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_fill_rate_parity(cpp):
    storage = [300.0, 350.0, 330.0, 380.0]
    got = cpp.fill_rate(storage)
    expected = _py_fill_rate(storage)
    assert math.isnan(got[0])
    assert all(_close(g, e) for g, e in zip(got[1:], expected[1:]))


def test_fill_rate_single_element(cpp):
    got = cpp.fill_rate([500.0])
    assert len(got) == 1
    assert math.isnan(got[0])


# ─── fetch_eia (unit / caching) ───────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_fetch_eia_raises_without_key():
    from oil_alpha.data.sources import fetch_eia
    from oil_alpha.data.budget import APIBudget

    env_backup = os.environ.pop("EIA_API_KEY", None)
    try:
        with pytest.raises(EnvironmentError, match="EIA_API_KEY"):
            fetch_eia("PET.WCSSTUS1.W", "2023-01-01", "2023-12-31", budget=APIBudget())
    finally:
        if env_backup is not None:
            os.environ["EIA_API_KEY"] = env_backup

"""Streamlit dashboard for the CL-vs-XLE lead-lag study.

Run:  ``streamlit run app/dashboard.py``

Shows live pipeline *progress*, a *results* panel (CCF curve, Granger p-values,
cointegration verdict, rolling corr/beta), and a *costs* panel with the three
flavours the user asked for: API free-tier budget, hypothetical transaction
cost, and per-stage compute time.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys

# Make ``src`` importable when run via ``streamlit run app/dashboard.py``.
_SRC = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "src")
if _SRC not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(_SRC))

import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
import plotly.graph_objects as go  # noqa: E402
import streamlit as st  # noqa: E402

from oil_alpha.config import DEFAULT_START, LAG, LEAD, SYMBOLS, RunConfig, default_end  # noqa: E402
from oil_alpha.pipeline import ProgressEvent, run_pipeline  # noqa: E402

st.set_page_config(page_title="Crude-Oil Lead-Lag Lab", layout="wide")
st.title("🛢️ Crude-Oil Lead-Lag Lab")
st.caption(
    f"Does **{SYMBOLS[LEAD]} (WTI futures)** lead **{SYMBOLS[LAG]} (energy ETF)**? "
    "Daily study per the crude-oil research paper, Stages 1-3."
)

# --- Sidebar: run controls ---------------------------------------------------
with st.sidebar:
    st.header("Run settings")
    start = st.text_input("Start date", DEFAULT_START)
    end = st.text_input("End date", default_end())
    return_kind = st.radio("Return type", ["log", "simple"], horizontal=True)
    max_lag = st.slider("Max lag (trading days)", 1, 30, 10)
    rolling_window = st.slider("Rolling window", 20, 120, 60, step=10)
    drop_roll_days = st.checkbox("Drop CL=F roll-day jumps", value=True)
    use_cache = st.checkbox("Use local cache", value=True)
    turnover = st.number_input("Hypothetical turnover / yr", 1.0, 1000.0, 252.0, step=10.0)
    run = st.button("▶ Run pipeline", type="primary", use_container_width=True)
    st.markdown(
        "<small>yfinance + FRED need no API key. Negative-price (Apr-2020) and "
        "roll-day traps are handled automatically.</small>",
        unsafe_allow_html=True,
    )


def _ccf_figure(ll) -> go.Figure:
    fig = go.Figure()
    fig.add_bar(x=ll.lags, y=ll.ccf, name="CCF")
    fig.add_vline(x=ll.peak_lag, line_dash="dash", line_color="crimson")
    fig.add_annotation(
        x=ll.peak_lag, y=ll.peak_corr,
        text=f"peak lag {ll.peak_lag}", showarrow=True, arrowhead=2,
    )
    fig.update_layout(
        title=f"Cross-correlation  ρ(k)=corr({ll.x_name}ₜ, {ll.y_name}ₜ₊ₖ)   (k>0 ⇒ {ll.x_name} leads)",
        xaxis_title="lag k (days)", yaxis_title="correlation", height=340,
        margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=50, b=10),
    )
    return fig


def _line(series: pd.Series, title: str, yaxis: str) -> go.Figure:
    fig = go.Figure()
    fig.add_scatter(x=series.index, y=series.to_numpy(), mode="lines")
    fig.update_layout(title=title, yaxis_title=yaxis, height=300, margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=40, b=10))
    return fig


def _render_results(result) -> None:
    ll = result.leadlag
    st.subheader("Results")

    c1, c2, c3 = st.columns(3)
    leader = "CL (futures)" if ll.x_leads else ("XLE" if ll.peak_lag < 0 else "contemporaneous")
    c1.metric("Lead-lag leader", leader, f"peak lag {ll.peak_lag}")
    if result.granger:
        g = result.granger["x->y"]
        c2.metric(f"Granger {SYMBOLS[LEAD]}→{SYMBOLS[LAG]}", f"p={g.p_value:.3f}",
                  "significant" if g.significant else "n.s.")
    if result.spot_check:
        c3.metric("CL=F vs FRED spot", f"{result.spot_check['median_abs_pct']:.1f}%",
                  f"{result.spot_check['common_days']} common days")

    st.plotly_chart(_ccf_figure(ll), use_container_width=True)

    gc, cc = st.columns(2)
    with gc:
        st.markdown("**Granger causality (both directions)**")
        if result.granger:
            rows = [
                {"direction": g.direction, "best lag": g.best_lag,
                 "p-value": round(g.p_value, 4), "significant": g.significant}
                for g in result.granger.values()
            ]
            st.dataframe(pd.DataFrame(rows), hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)
            st.caption("Granger = predictive precedence, not true causation (paper Part 2.3).")
    with cc:
        st.markdown("**Cointegration (price levels)**")
        if result.eg_coint:
            st.write("•", result.eg_coint.verdict)
        if result.johansen_coint:
            st.write("•", result.johansen_coint.verdict)

    rc, rb = st.columns(2)
    if result.rolling_corr is not None and not result.rolling_corr.empty:
        rc.plotly_chart(
            _line(result.rolling_corr, f"Rolling correlation ({SYMBOLS[LEAD]} vs {SYMBOLS[LAG]})", "corr"),
            use_container_width=True,
        )
    if result.rolling_beta is not None and not result.rolling_beta.empty:
        rb.plotly_chart(
            _line(result.rolling_beta, f"Rolling β of {SYMBOLS[LAG]} to oil", "beta"),
            use_container_width=True,
        )

    if result.warnings:
        for w in result.warnings:
            st.warning(w)


def _render_costs(result) -> None:
    st.subheader("Projected costs")
    a, b, c = st.tabs(["① API free-tier budget", "② Transaction cost", "③ Compute / time"])

    with a:
        rows = result.budget.as_rows()
        if rows:
            df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
            st.dataframe(df, hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)
            for r in rows:
                if r["cap"] is not None:
                    st.progress(min(1.0, r["fraction"] or 0.0),
                                text=f"{r['source']}: {r['used']}/{r['cap']} used")
        st.caption(f"Total requests this run: {result.budget.total_requests()} "
                   "(yfinance/FRED have no hard cap; capped sources shown with bars).")

    with b:
        if result.cost_estimates:
            df = pd.DataFrame([
                {"asset": SYMBOLS.get(c.asset_key, c.asset_key),
                 "round-trip (bp)": round(c.round_trip_bp, 2),
                 "turnover/yr": c.turnover_per_year,
                 "annual drag (bp)": round(c.annual_drag_bp, 1),
                 "annual drag (%)": round(c.annual_drag_pct, 2)}
                for c in result.cost_estimates
            ])
            st.dataframe(df, hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)
        st.caption("Illustrative half-spread + commission assumptions (config.COST_MODEL), "
                   "not calibrated to live quotes.")

    with c:
        if result.metrics:
            st.dataframe(pd.DataFrame(result.metrics.as_rows()), hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)
            st.metric("Total compute time", f"{result.metrics.total_seconds:.2f} s")


def _run(cfg: RunConfig) -> None:
    progress = st.progress(0.0, text="starting…")
    with st.status("Running pipeline…", expanded=True) as status:
        final = None
        for event in run_pipeline(cfg):
            progress.progress(event.pct, text=f"{event.stage} — {event.message}")
            icon = {"ok": "✅", "warn": "⚠️", "error": "❌", "done": "🏁"}.get(event.status, "•")
            if event.status != "start":
                st.write(f"{icon} **{event.stage}** — {event.message}")
            if event.stage == "done":
                final = event.payload
        status.update(label="Pipeline complete", state="complete")
    st.session_state["result"] = final


if run:
    cfg = RunConfig(
        start=start, end=end, return_kind=return_kind, max_lag=max_lag,
        rolling_window=rolling_window, drop_roll_days=drop_roll_days,
        use_cache=use_cache, turnover_per_year=turnover,
    )
    _run(cfg)

result = st.session_state.get("result")
if result is not None and result.leadlag is not None:
    _render_results(result)
    st.divider()
    _render_costs(result)
elif result is not None:
